headline: Advance Lodging and Winter Road Status Check
reservation: Crater Lake entry requires a park pass, which can be purchased at the gate or online; lodging at Crater Lake Lodge or Mazama Village requires separate bookings made months ahead. During the summer, boat tour reservations are a separate bottleneck and require a steep hike to reach. Check the official NPS site for changing seasonal road closures that affect north and south entrance access.

days.title: The Rim and Volcanic Vistas

stops.name: Sinnott Memorial Overlook
stops.detail: Visit the indoor museum perched on the caldera cliff for a geologic orientation and steep lake views.

stops.name: Discovery Point Trail
stops.detail: Walk the easy 2-mile round trip along the rim for views of Wizard Island where the lake was first documented.

days.driving: Local rim driving; allow 1 hour for slow speeds and frequent stops
days.note: High elevation means snow can block sections of this route even in early July.

days.title: East Rim Drive and High Peaks

stops.name: Watchman Peak Trail
stops.detail: Ascend the moderate trail to a historic fire lookout for a 360-degree panorama of the Cascades.

stops.name: Phantom Ship Overlook
stops.detail: View the oldest rock formation in the lake, which resembles a ghost ship, from the roadside pull-off.

days.driving: Allow 3-4 hours to complete the full 33-mile Rim Drive loop; conditions vary
days.note: Watchman Peak is a popular spot for afternoon clouds; check visibility before the climb.

days.title: Lakeshore Access and Pinnacles
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the North Entrance

stops.name: Cleetwood Cove Trail
stops.detail: Descend the only legal path to the water's edge, keeping in mind the 700-foot elevation gain on the return.

stops.name: The Pinnacles
stops.detail: Drive to the park's southeast corner to see volcanic ash spires eroded into needle-like formations.

days.driving: Significant distance between sites; allow 2 hours for travel between Cleetwood and Pinnacles
days.note: Lakeshore access is physically demanding; ensure everyone is prepared for a steep, dusty ascent.

intel.title: Rim Village Congestion
intel.text: Parking lots at Rim Village and Cleetwood Cove often fill by midday in peak August. Arrive before 10 AM to secure a spot near the main visitor services.

intel.title: Caldera Connectivity
intel.text: Expect near-total signal loss inside the caldera and on many backcountry trails. Print your reservation confirmations and park maps before entering the park boundaries.

intel.title: Strategic Refueling
intel.text: Mazama Village offers the only seasonal fuel within the park. If arriving from Medford or Klamath Falls, ensure you have a full tank to cover the high-altitude driving loops.

intel.title: Short Summer Window
intel.text: The full Rim Drive typically only opens from July through September. Outside this window, travel is restricted to the south entrance and Rim Village area.

intel.title: Road Closure Alerts
intel.text: The North Entrance road closes annually with the first significant snow, often in October or November. Always check the official NPS 'Roads' page for daily status updates.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at Rogue Valley (MFR) and shop for water and snacks in Medford. Allow 2 hours for the drive to the park's southern gate.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for paved rim roads, but ensure your rental allows for mountain grades; RVs face length restrictions on specific narrow East Rim curves.
plan.goldenHour: Cloudcap Overlook is the highest point on the road and offers expansive eastern views for sunrise, seasonal road access permitting.
